the use of statins does not impede exercise tolerance and that exercise training potentiates its insulin-sensitising effects.
the use of statins in combination with exercise training improves insulin sensitivity in elderly obese males, with and without Type II diabetes.
exercise training improves insulin sensitivity and mitochondrial oxidative capacity, and this effect is more prominent in statin users than in control subjects.

the effect of exercise training on cardiometabolic risk in elderly obese males with and those without Type 2 diabetic mellitus and the role that statins play in this process.
the use of statins in the treatment of insulin resistance.
the effects of exercise training and the use of statins on mitochondrial function, glucose metabolism and insulin sensitivity.

the use of statins potentiated the insulin-sensitized effect of exercise training.
the combination of statins and exercise training is beneficial for the prevention and treatment of cardiometabolic risk.
the use of statins in combination with progressive exercise training potentiates the improvement of cardiometabolic risk and insulin sensitivity.

the use of statins does not impede exercise training performance or tolerance, but rather potentiates the training-induced improvements in cardiometablic risk factors, especially insulin sensitivity.
